name: Button
summary: Makes something happen on the page, such as sending a code or going on to the next step. It's never disabled: if something's missing, pressing it says what.

when: To do something: continue, send, save or confirm.
To submit a form. Use one primary button per step, for the main thing people came to do.

whenNot.text: To go to another page or site.
For an action with only an icon, such as closing the sheet.
To sign in or create an account from an app.

anatomy.description: The shape people press. At least 44px in both directions.
Before or after the label. Decorative: the label names the button.
Says what happens, starting with a verb.
A spinner shown while busy. Its speed comes from the motion tokens, so it stops for reduced motion.

values.description: The one main action on a step.
Other actions, beside or below the primary one.
Low-emphasis actions that look like links, such as “Try another provider”.

props.name: type
props.description: What it does in a form. Doras buttons only submit when asked to, so a new button never submits a form by accident.

values.description: Does nothing in a form; the app handles the press.
Resets its form. Rarely right: people lose what they typed.

props.name: busy
props.description: Shows that something is happening, such as checking a handle. While busy, presses do nothing.

props.name: busyLabel
props.description: What it says while busy, such as “Checking…”. Without one, the label stays and the spinner shows.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fills the width of its container, as at the foot of the sheet.

states.name: Hover
states.description: The surface changes to its hover colour.

states.name: Focus
states.description: A 2px focus ring, 2px away from the button.

states.name: Busy
states.description: The busy label and spinner show, and presses do nothing until it's done.

events.name: click
events.when: It's pressed, by pointer, keyboard or assistive technology, and isn't busy. A submit button also submits its form.

accessibility.name: Its label. Icons are hidden from screen readers.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to it, in reading order.

screenReader: Announced as a button, with its label.
While busy, its name becomes the busy label, and pressing it again does nothing.
announcements: When it becomes busy, its busy label is announced politely through the shared announcer.
notes: Never disabled. A disabled button can't be focused or explain itself, so people can't tell what's wrong (decision in #1).
Its target is at least 44px by 44px (WCAG 2.5.5).
Its focus ring is at least 2px, with 3:1 contrast in every theme (WCAG 2.4.13).
In forced colours it uses the system's button colours, and its focus ring stays visible.

related.relationship: For actions with only an icon.
For going somewhere, not doing something.
The one door into signing in, with its own look.
Says what's missing when a submit button is pressed too soon.
For showing and hiding content, rather than doing something.

guidelines: Start with a verb that says what happens, such as “Send the code” or “Continue”.
Use sentence case, and no full stop.
Never “Submit”, “OK” or “Click here”: they don't say what happens.
Busy labels say what's happening, and end with an ellipsis: “Checking…”.
Keep labels short. They must fit in German and the pseudo-locale, which are about 40% longer.

dosAndDonts.do: Keep the button pressable, and say what's missing when it's pressed.
dosAndDonts.dont: Disable it until the form is complete.

dosAndDonts.do: Use one primary button per step.
dosAndDonts.dont: Put two primary buttons side by side.

dosAndDonts.do: Use a link to go to another page.

evidence.point: Disabled buttons give no reason and can't be focused, so people using screen readers can miss them entirely.

source.label: GOV.UK Design System: avoid disabled buttons

evidence.point: Targets of at least 44px help people with tremors and people using touch.
A visible, thick focus ring helps keyboard users see where they are.
Buttons default to type button, not submit as native buttons do, so adding one to a form never submits it by accident.
